title: Judges Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 17.

questions.question: Who was the man from mount Ephraim mentioned in Judges 17?
questions.correctAnswer: Micah
questions.explanation: Judges 17:1 states that the man of mount Ephraim was named Micah.

questions.question: How much silver did Micah admit to taking from his mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Eleven hundred shekels
questions.explanation: Judges 17:2 records that Micah said he took eleven hundred shekels of silver from his mother.

questions.question: What did Micah's mother originally dedicate the silver for?
options: To make a graven image and a molten image
questions.correctAnswer: To make a graven image and a molten image
questions.explanation: Judges 17:3 explains that Micah's mother dedicated the silver to the LORD to make a graven and molten image.

questions.question: How much silver did Micah's mother give to the founder to make the images?
questions.correctAnswer: Two hundred shekels
questions.explanation: Judges 17:4 states that she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave it to the founder to make the images.

questions.question: What items did Micah have in his house of gods?
options: An ephod, teraphim, and a priest
An ephod, teraphim, and a graven image
An ephod, teraphim, and a molten image
An ephod, teraphim, and a priest consecrated from his sons
questions.correctAnswer: An ephod, teraphim, and a priest consecrated from his sons
questions.explanation: Judges 17:5 says Micah had an house of gods, made an ephod and teraphim, and consecrated one of his sons as priest.

questions.question: True or False: In Judges 17, Micah consecrated a Levite from Bethlehem as his priest.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 17:5 and 17:12 show Micah consecrated one of his sons as priest; the Levite came later and was made priest by Micah, but not consecrated by him initially.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter states there was no king in Israel at that time.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 clearly says there was no king in Israel in those days.

questions.question: From which city did the young Levite come?
questions.correctAnswer: Bethlehemjudah
questions.explanation: Judges 17:7 mentions the young Levite was from Bethlehemjudah.

questions.question: What did Micah offer the Levite to live with him and be his priest?
options: Ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of apparel, and victuals
questions.correctAnswer: Ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of apparel, and victuals
questions.explanation: Judges 17:10 says Micah offered the Levite ten shekels of silver yearly, a suit of apparel, and food.

questions.question: What was Micah's feeling after the Levite became his priest?
options: He was confident the LORD would do him good
questions.correctAnswer: He was confident the LORD would do him good
questions.explanation: Judges 17:13 says Micah believed the LORD would do him good because he had a Levite as his priest.

questions.question: True or False: Micah restored the full amount of the silver to his mother before she used some to make images.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 17:3-4 shows Micah restored the full eleven hundred shekels, and then his mother took two hundred shekels to make images.

questions.question: What type of images were made with the silver?
questions.correctAnswer: Graven and molten images
questions.explanation: Judges 17:3-4 states the silver was used to make a graven image and a molten image.

questions.question: What did the Levite do when Micah invited him to stay and be his priest?
options: He was content to dwell with Micah
questions.correctAnswer: He was content to dwell with Micah
questions.explanation: Judges 17:11 states the Levite was content to dwell with Micah and became like a son to him.

questions.question: True or False: The house of Micah contained an ephod and teraphim.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 17:5 explicitly says Micah made an ephod and teraphim in his house of gods.

questions.question: In Judges 17, what happened first?
options: Micah consecrated his son as priest
Micah restored the silver to his mother
The Levite arrived at Micah's house
The graven and molten images were made
questions.correctAnswer: Micah restored the silver to his mother
questions.explanation: According to the chapter sequence, Micah first restored the silver to his mother (v2-3), then the images were made (v4), Micah consecrated his son (v5), and later the Levite arrived (v7-8).

medium.title: Judges Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Judges 17:6 teach us about leadership during the time of Micah?
options: There was a king who ruled Israel wisely
Every man did what was right in his own eyes
There was peace and unity under one leader
questions.correctAnswer: Every man did what was right in his own eyes
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 states, 'In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes,' indicating a lack of centralized leadership and moral relativism.

questions.question: According to Judges 17:7, from which town did the young Levite come?
questions.correctAnswer: Bethlehemjudah
questions.explanation: Judges 17:7 specifically mentions the young Levite was from Bethlehemjudah of the family of Judah.

questions.question: What motivated the Levite to leave Bethlehemjudah according to Judges 17:8?
options: He was banished by the elders
He sought a place to sojourn
He was called to be a king
He wanted to find a wife
questions.correctAnswer: He sought a place to sojourn
questions.explanation: Judges 17:8 states the Levite departed Bethlehemjudah to sojourn where he could find a place, indicating he was looking for a dwelling or position.

questions.question: In Judges 17:9, how does the Levite identify himself to Micah?
options: A Levite of Bethlehemjudah seeking a place to sojourn
questions.correctAnswer: A Levite of Bethlehemjudah seeking a place to sojourn
questions.explanation: Judges 17:9 records the Levite saying, 'I am a Levite of Bethlehemjudah, and I go to sojourn where I may find a place,' showing his identity and purpose.

questions.question: What offer did Micah make to the Levite in Judges 17:10?
options: To give him land and a title
To make him king of Ephraim
To make him his father and priest with payment and provision
To send him back to Bethlehemjudah
questions.correctAnswer: To make him his father and priest with payment and provision
questions.explanation: Judges 17:10 shows Micah inviting the Levite to dwell with him and be his father and priest, promising ten shekels of silver annually, apparel, and food.

questions.question: How does Judges 17:11 describe the Levite's response to Micah's offer?
options: He was content to dwell with Micah and became like a son to him
questions.correctAnswer: He was content to dwell with Micah and became like a son to him
questions.explanation: Judges 17:11 states the Levite was content to dwell with Micah and was like one of his sons, showing acceptance and close relationship.

questions.question: What action did Micah take in Judges 17:12 after the Levite agreed to stay?
options: He consecrated the Levite as his priest
He built a temple for the Levite
questions.correctAnswer: He consecrated the Levite as his priest
questions.explanation: Judges 17:12 says Micah consecrated the Levite, who then became his priest and served in Micah's house.

questions.question: According to Judges 17:13, what was Micah's belief about having a Levite as his priest?
options: That it would bring him harm
That the LORD would do him good
That he would become a king
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD would do him good
questions.explanation: Judges 17:13 records Micah saying, 'Now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest,' showing his confidence in divine blessing.

questions.question: What does the passage from Judges 17:6-10 teach about leadership and spiritual authority in Israel at the time?
options: There was strong centralized leadership with clear obedience
People acted according to their own judgment without a king
questions.correctAnswer: People acted according to their own judgment without a king
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 shows no king existed and everyone did what was right in their own eyes; verses 7-10 illustrate how a Levite could be hired as priest, highlighting decentralized and informal leadership.

questions.question: Based on Judges 17:10 and 17:13, what might Micah's hiring of the Levite reveal about his faith and trust in God?
options: Micah trusted the LORD would bless him through the Levite's priesthood
Micah wanted to rebel against God
questions.correctAnswer: Micah trusted the LORD would bless him through the Levite's priesthood
questions.explanation: In Judges 17:10 Micah offers to pay the Levite as priest, and in 17:13 he expresses confidence that the LORD will do him good because he has a Levite priest, showing trust in divine blessing.

questions.question: How does Judges 17:6-11 illustrate the importance of integrity in spiritual matters?
options: It shows people strictly obeyed God's commands without question
It demonstrates the chaos when individuals define right by their own standards
It shows the Levites had complete authority
It illustrates the unity of Israel under God's law
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates the chaos when individuals define right by their own standards
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 explains there was no king and everyone did what was right in their own eyes, while 7-11 show Micah hiring a Levite to serve as priest, reflecting personal and possibly misguided religious practice.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 17:7, the young man from Bethlehemjudah was a Levite by tribe and traveled seeking a place to live.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 17:7 states the young man was a Levite from Bethlehemjudah who sojourned there, implying he was traveling to find a place.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 17:12 reveals that Micah appointed his own son as priest instead of the Levite.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 17:12 indicates Micah consecrated the Levite as his priest; although verse 5 mentions Micah consecrated one of his sons earlier, the passage here focuses on the Levite's priesthood.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 17:8-9, the Levite's journey to Mount Ephraim was purposeful to find a role with Micah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 17:8-9 show the Levite was seeking any place to sojourn and happened to come to Micah's house; it was not a purposeful search specifically for Micah.

questions.question: According to Judges 17:4-5, what religious items did Micah make and keep in his house?
options: An ephod, teraphim, and a graven image
A scroll of the law and altars
A golden calf and incense altar
A tabernacle and ark of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: An ephod, teraphim, and a graven image
questions.explanation: Judges 17:4-5 describe Micah making a graven image and molten image, an ephod, and teraphim, which he kept in his house.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 17.

questions.question: What role did the Levite assume in Micah's house?
questions.correctAnswer: Priest
questions.explanation: Judges 17:12 states that Micah consecrated the Levite and the young man became his priest in the house of Micah.

questions.question: According to Judges 17, why did Micah believe the LORD would do him good?
options: Because he had a Levite as his priest
questions.correctAnswer: Because he had a Levite as his priest
questions.explanation: Judges 17:13 shows Micah's confidence in receiving good from the LORD because he had a Levite to be his priest.

questions.question: How did Micah treat the Levite who came from Bethlehemjudah?
questions.correctAnswer: As one of his sons
questions.explanation: Judges 17:11 explains that the Levite was content to dwell with Micah and was unto him as one of his sons.

questions.question: What payment did Micah offer the Levite for serving as his priest?
options: Ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of apparel, and victuals
One hundred shekels of silver per year
questions.correctAnswer: Ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of apparel, and victuals
questions.explanation: Judges 17:10 details Micah's offer of ten shekels of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and food to the Levite.

questions.question: From which tribe was the young Levite who came to Micah's house?
questions.correctAnswer: Levi
questions.explanation: Judges 17:7 identifies the young man as a Levite from Bethlehemjudah of the family of Judah.

questions.question: What was Micah's attitude toward the silver taken from his mother?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 17:2 shows Micah admitting he took the eleven hundred shekels and returning them to his mother, indicating honesty.

questions.question: In Judges 17:6, what is said about the leadership situation in Israel at that time?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 states there was no king in Israel, and everyone did what was right in their own eyes, indicating a lack of centralized leadership.

questions.question: What objects did Micah have in his house that are mentioned in Judges 17?
options: An ephod, teraphim, and graven images
questions.correctAnswer: An ephod, teraphim, and graven images
questions.explanation: Judges 17:5 describes that Micah had an ephod, teraphim, and graven images in his house.

questions.question: Which verse in Judges 17 highlights the social and religious chaos in Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Judges 17:6
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 states there was no king in Israel, and everyone did what was right in his own eyes, reflecting social and religious disorder.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book echoes the theme of 'no king in Israel' and everyone doing what was right in their own eyes?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8 discusses Israel's demand for a king due to the failures of judges, echoing the theme of Judges 17:6 about lack of centralized leadership.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'consecrated' used in Judges 17:12 carries what implication?
options: To dedicate or set apart for holy use
questions.correctAnswer: To dedicate or set apart for holy use
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root for 'consecrated' (קדש, qādash) means to set apart or sanctify, as seen in Judges 17:12 where Micah consecrates the Levite as priest.

questions.question: The relationship between Micah and the Levite can be best described as which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Judges 17:11 uses 'as one of his sons' to describe the Levite's relationship to Micah, which is a simile comparing the Levite to a son.

questions.question: How does the episode of Micah and the Levite foreshadow later issues in Israel's religious history?
options: It foreshadows the establishment of the true priesthood under Aaron
It foreshadows the monarchy under Saul
It foreshadows the building of Solomon's temple
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the establishment of the true priesthood under Aaron
questions.explanation: The improper priesthood here (Judges 17:12) contrasts with the legitimate Aaronic priesthood established in Exodus and Leviticus, highlighting religious confusion before centralized worship.

questions.question: What cultural practice does Micah's making of a graven image and molten image reflect, according to Judges 17?
questions.correctAnswer: Ancient Near Eastern idolatry
questions.explanation: Judges 17:4 describes the making of graven and molten images, which reflects common idolatrous practices in the ancient Near East contrary to Israelite law.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the principle that 'every man did that which was right in his own eyes' leading to chaos, as seen in Judges 17:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 1:21-25
questions.explanation: Romans 1:21-25 describes humanity's rejection of God's truth leading to idolatry and moral chaos, paralleling the lawlessness in Judges 17:6.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Micah's restoration of the silver to his mother and her subsequent use of part of it to make idols illustrate about human sinfulness and idolatry?
options: A willingness to honor God fully
A distorted worship replacing God with created things
A clear rejection of material possessions
questions.correctAnswer: A distorted worship replacing God with created things
questions.explanation: Judges 17:2-4 show that although the silver was returned, the mother used it to create graven and molten images, highlighting idolatry and the human tendency to substitute created things for true worship of God.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Micah appointing his son as a priest despite the Levitical regulations for priesthood?
options: The doctrine of the priesthood of all believers
The doctrine of human corruption in religious practices
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of human corruption in religious practices
questions.explanation: Judges 17:5 reveals Micah consecrated his son as a priest, violating God’s ordained Levitical priesthood and illustrating human corruption and deviation from God’s covenantal law.

questions.question: How does Judges 17:6 contribute to the understanding of the spiritual condition of Israel during the period of the Judges?
options: Israel had a strong centralized government
There was moral and religious relativism without divine guidance
The people strictly followed the Mosaic Law
The nation experienced peace and unity
questions.correctAnswer: There was moral and religious relativism without divine guidance
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states 'In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes,' showing the absence of godly leadership led to moral relativism and lawlessness.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's providence can be drawn from the Levite’s journey from Bethlehemjudah to Micah’s house?
options: God’s providence is evident even in human wandering
God allows evil to triumph without intervention
God’s covenant is limited to the tribe of Judah
God directly commands every human action
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence is evident even in human wandering
questions.explanation: Judges 17:7-8 shows the Levite wandering and eventually settling with Micah, which reflects God's providential guidance within human freedom, even amid spiritual confusion.

questions.question: What does Micah’s offer to the Levite (ten shekels, apparel, and victuals) reveal about the nature of religious service in this context?
options: Religious service was freely given without compensation
Religious service was commercialized and contractual
Priests were supported solely by voluntary offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Religious service was commercialized and contractual
questions.explanation: Judges 17:10 indicates that Micah offered payment and provisions for the Levite’s priestly service, revealing a transactional and corrupt approach to worship contrary to divine appointment.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is indirectly challenged by the presence of idols and unauthorized priests in Micah’s house?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness
questions.explanation: Judges 17:5 and 17:4 highlight idolatry and unauthorized priesthood, which violate God's holy nature, showing human disregard for His holiness (Lev 19:2).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Judges 17:5 and Judges 17:12 teach about legitimate worship and priesthood?
options: Priesthood is based on family lineage and personal choice
Legitimate worship requires adherence to God's prescribed order
All individuals have equal authority to officiate worship
Worship is valid regardless of the officiant’s identity
questions.correctAnswer: Legitimate worship requires adherence to God's prescribed order
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 12 show Micah consecrating his son and later the Levite as priests, which was unauthorized, teaching that true worship requires obedience to God’s lawful priesthood (Exodus 28).

questions.question: How does Judges 17:6's statement about there being no king in Israel relate to the need for Christ as King in the biblical narrative?
options: It reveals the consequences of lacking God’s sovereign rule
It shows that kingship was unnecessary in Israel
It predicts the rise of earthly kings only
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the consequences of lacking God’s sovereign rule
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 presents the chaos from lack of kingly authority, pointing forward to Christ as the ultimate King who brings righteous governance (Revelation 19:16).

questions.question: What do the actions of Micah and his mother teach about the human tendency towards syncretism in worship?
options: They combined elements of true worship with idolatry
They rejected any form of religious images
They focused solely on spiritual worship without objects
questions.correctAnswer: They combined elements of true worship with idolatry
questions.explanation: Judges 17:3-4 shows the mother dedicating silver to the LORD but using it to make idols, illustrating syncretism—mixing true worship with forbidden practices.

questions.question: What does the narrative of the Levite from Bethlehemjudah choosing to sojourn with Micah reveal about the religious authority in Israel during this time?
options: Religious authority was centralized and well-ordered
Levites sought legitimate priestly appointments from the temple
Religious authority was fragmented and often self-appointed
There was no need for Levites to serve as priests
questions.correctAnswer: Religious authority was fragmented and often self-appointed
questions.explanation: Judges 17:7-9 depict the Levite wandering and accepting Micah’s offer, indicating a breakdown of religious order and the rise of self-appointed priests.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the chaotic religious practices described in Judges 17:1-13 prove that the Old Testament God was indifferent to idolatry and moral order. What does this passage actually teach about God's character and human responsibility?
options: God condones idolatry and human moral autonomy
God's holiness is violated by human sin, but He allows free will consequences
God is powerless to prevent idolatry
God directly commands idolatry in this period
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness is violated by human sin, but He allows free will consequences
questions.explanation: Judges 17:6 and surrounding verses show human rebellion and idolatry, reflecting God’s holiness contrasted with human sin and free will, not divine indifference (Isaiah 59:2).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is emphasized by the fact that Micah's Levite priest was 'content to dwell' with him and acted as a son (Judges 17:11)?
options: The doctrine of divine calling is irrelevant
Human desires can shape religious roles, not divine calling
Priestly office is based on divine election only
questions.correctAnswer: Human desires can shape religious roles, not divine calling
questions.explanation: Judges 17:11 shows the Levite accepting the role out of convenience or human ties rather than divine commissioning, emphasizing human influence in corrupted religious practices.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Judges 17:2-3 and Judges 17:13 provide about human attempts at securing divine blessing through improper means?
options: Human schemes to gain favor often misunderstand God's holiness
God blesses all who dedicate offerings regardless of form
Blessing is unrelated to worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: Human schemes to gain favor often misunderstand God's holiness
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 reveal the mother’s dedication of silver to make idols, and verse 13 shows Micah's belief that having a Levite priest ensures blessing, both reflect misunderstanding of true worship and God's holiness.

questions.question: How does the presence of teraphim and an ephod in Micah’s house (Judges 17:5) illustrate the syncretism and religious confusion in Israel during the Judges period?
options: They represent pure adherence to Yahweh worship
They indicate mixing of pagan objects with Israelite religious symbols
They are exclusively associated with the tabernacle worship
They were universally rejected by all Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: They indicate mixing of pagan objects with Israelite religious symbols
questions.explanation: Judges 17:5 mentions teraphim (household idols) alongside an ephod, showing syncretism by mixing pagan and Israelite religious items, reflecting confusion in worship.

questions.question: What does Judges 17:1-4 and 17:10-12 teach about the relationship between material wealth and spiritual corruption?
options: Material wealth always leads to true worship
Material wealth can be a source of idolatry and spiritual corruption
Spiritual leaders never seek material gain
Material wealth is irrelevant to spiritual practices
questions.correctAnswer: Material wealth can be a source of idolatry and spiritual corruption
questions.explanation: The silver was used for idols (17:2-4) and Micah paid the Levite for priestly service (17:10-12), demonstrating how material wealth can facilitate idolatry and corrupt worship.
